{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement client-side changes so the UI and requests use the new server-side sort enum and never perform per-page-only reordering.

Requirements for the frontend implementation:
- UI: Add two sort options (exact values to send to server): "created_at_desc" and "title_asc". Present these exact token strings to the request layer; the visible labels may be localized but must map to those exact values.
- Parameter usage: Include a query parameter named sort with the chosen enum value on every list fetch and on every pagination navigation (next/prev/page links). Do not rely on client-only reordering of the currently loaded page to satisfy user selection. Always request the server with the requested sort to get globally consistent ordering.
- Default behavior: Do not rely on implicit client-only defaults. Either (a) explicitly send sort=created_at_desc on initial list fetches, or (b) if you omit the sort parameter, expect the server default to be created_at_desc; however, the safest implementation is to include sort in every request so pagination links can include the same value.
- Pagination links and stored state: Ensure all server pagination links, programmatic page requests, and stored list state include the current sort value so subsequent pages use the same server-side ordering.
- Error handling: If the server returns HTTP 422 for an invalid sort value, surface the error to the user (show a message) and set the UI sort control to a valid value. Do not silently ignore or locally reorder results. If the UI accidentally sent an invalid value, set the control to a valid choice (recommend: created_at_desc) after informing the user.
- Filtering: Preserve all existing filter behaviors. Ensure filters are sent unchanged alongside the sort parameter.

Acceptance tests for the frontend:
- When user selects "created_at_desc" or "title_asc", every fetch (including subsequent pages) sends sort=<value> to the server.
- Pagination requests include the same sort value as the current list view.
- The UI never reorders the entries of the current page in JavaScript to pretend global sorting — observed behavior: items on a page reflect the server response order only.
- When server responds 422, the UI shows the error and sets the sort control to a valid value rather than silently reordering results.
- Filters remain identical to previous behavior and are included in every request along with sort.

Notes to implementer: Do not implement client-side algorithms that attempt to reproduce server sort semantics; rely on server-side sorting + pagination for correctness."
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Implement server-side validation, sorting and pagination updates to support two new sort enum values and the specified tie-break and null placement rules.

API contract (apply exactly):
- Allowed sort values: exactly the strings "created_at_desc" and "title_asc".
- Default when the sort parameter is absent: treat as "created_at_desc".
- If the request provides a sort parameter with any other value: respond with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity and a structured error indicating invalid sort value. Do not silently accept or map other values.

Sorting behavior (must be applied before pagination):
- Always perform server-side sorting on the full result set after filters are applied and before pagination is applied. The server MUST sort then paginate (i.e., ORDER/LIST -> SORT -> PAGINATE -> RETURN page).
- For sort = "created_at_desc":
  - Primary key: created_at in descending order (newest first).
  - NULL handling: Any row with created_at = NULL must be placed after non-NULL rows (i.e., NULLs last in the descending order).
  - Tie-breaker: when created_at values compare equal, order by the resource UUID canonical lowercase string in ascending order (i.e., compare lowercased UUID strings lexicographically ascending). Use the canonical UUID column on your resource (do not invent a different field); ensure comparison is performed on the lowercase normalization of that UUID string.
- For sort = "title_asc":
  - Primary key: title ascending in Unicode code point (scalar) order (NOT locale-aware collation). Implement using a stable binary/unicode-code-point comparison so ordering is by Unicode code point numeric order.
  - Tie-breaker: when title values compare equal, order by the resource UUID canonical lowercase string in ascending order (same rule as above).

Implementation guidance (do not invent DB names; use your schema's created_at/title/UUID columns as described):
- SQL / ORM guidance:
  - Ensure sorting expression equals: primary sort expression, then tie-breaker lower(uuid) ASC. For created_at_desc you must also ensure NULLs appear last. Example patterns (adjust to your schema and SQL dialect):
    - PostgreSQL example: ORDER BY (created_at IS NULL) ASC, created_at DESC, lower(uuid_column) ASC
    - MySQL example: ORDER BY (created_at IS NULL) ASC, created_at DESC, LCASE(uuid_column) ASC
  - For title Unicode code point ordering, choose a binary/code-point collation for the title column comparison. Examples:
    - PostgreSQL: ORDER BY title COLLATE "C" ASC, lower(uuid_column) ASC
    - MySQL: ORDER BY title COLLATE utf8mb4_bin ASC, LCASE(uuid_column) ASC
  - If your DB/ORM cannot express Unicode code point order with a collation, implement a deterministic comparator that compares Unicode code points and use it in the ORDER BY stage (for example, create an indexed DB expression or perform comparison via a server-side function) — but the final ordering must be produced by the server before paginating.
- UUID tie-breaker details: compare the standard textual canonical representation in lowercase. If your UUID values are stored in binary or in mixed case, apply a lowercase normalization in the ORDER BY expression (e.g., lower(uuid::text) or LCASE(uuid_column)) so ordering matches canonical lowercase string ascending.

Validation and error handling:
- Param validation must be strict. If invalid, return 422 with a payload describing the invalid 'sort' value.
- If the server cannot honor Unicode code point ordering for title due to DB limitations, return a 500 and log details for fix; do not fallback to a different collation without an explicit change request.

Acceptance tests for the backend (must pass):
- Absent sort parameter: response is equivalent to sort=created_at_desc.
- sort parameter values other than the two allowed tokens trigger HTTP 422 and an error explaining the invalid sort value.
- For created_at_desc:
  - Non-NULL created_at rows appear before NULL created_at rows.
  - Rows are ordered newest->oldest for non-NULL created_at.
  - For rows with identical created_at values, ordering is ascending by the lowercase UUID string.
- For title_asc:
  - Rows are ordered ascending by title according to Unicode code point order.
  - For rows with identical title code-point sequences, ordering is ascending by the lowercase UUID string.
- Pagination: verify that sorting is applied to the entire filtered dataset before slicing pages; page N concatenated with page N+1 in the same sort yields a globally sorted sequence.
- Filtering unchanged: existing filtering rules produce the same filtered set prior to sorting/pagination.

Response metadata recommendation (to help frontend): include the applied sort value in response metadata (e.g., echo the effective sort token used) so the frontend can reliably preserve it across pagination. This is optional but recommended for robustness.

Do not change or assume any other contract not explicitly stated in these requirements."
  }
}
